newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam Jan-Aug trade gap record $3.25 bln -VNA.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam Jan-Aug trade gap record $3.25 bln -VNA.

text.p: Vietnam posted a record trade deficit of $3.25 billion in the first eight months of this year, the official Vietnam News Agency (VNA) said on Monday.

It said the trade deficit was fuelled by fast-growing imports, which rose by 45 percent from the same period of last year to $7.60 billion. Exports were $4.35 billion, up 22.6 percent from the first eight months of 1995.

The agency quoted government officials and major exporters as saying that although an export target of about $6.7 billion would be achieved this year, the trade deficit was not likely to be lower than $2.50 billion.
It said that $480 million of the exports in the first eight months was generated by foreign companies with investments in Vietnam, up 18.2 percent from the same period of 1995.
Exports of heavy industry and mining products increased by 24.4 percent, light industry and handicrafts by 31.1 percent, agro-forestry products by 21.1 percent and aquatic products by 4.8 percent.
Among staple exports, rice rose by 24.3 percent, textiles and footwear by 28.3 to 29 percent, crude oil by 10.5 percent and coffee and rubber 2.3 to 2.5 percent.
The import of machinery and equipment rose by 107 percent, materials and fuel by 30 percent, vehicles by 47.6 percent, cement by 32.2 percent, steel by 63 percent and motorbikes by 23 percent.
VNA said the import of consumer goods accounted for 10 percent of total imports, about 3.4 percent lower than the same period of 1995.
